**Charter-global defects that bear on this task.** Consequences demonstrated against this world:

- **CG-1** (undeclared override, carry clock anchor). `grain_evt_delivery_application` (in force, unoverridden) says the position date "is the date the carry clock starts from" — here 2025-11-14. `grain_ext_delayed_price_carry_charge`'s first anchor tier says the clock runs from the day the storage handling-shrink adjustment was taken — here `storage_charges.24f4222c-…`, `event_type` `storage_shrink_taken`, `charge_date` 2025-12-02. Recomputing on this world: under the extended anchor, `carry_days` = 87, `chargeable_days` = 57, `chargeable_months` = 1, charge = **90.19**; under the base anchor, `carry_days` = 105, `chargeable_days` = 75, `chargeable_months` = 2, charge = **180.39**. The two readings then propagate: the money released is **5624.30** on the first and **5534.10** on the second. Two defensible answers on the same world, from two clauses both in force.
- **CG-8** (the roll's prerequisite sentence resolves to two writes). A reader who resolves "the bushels still owed on the contract stand at the figure the loads applied to it support" to `register_contract_amendment_850dd44e` computes the balance by `grain_ext_delivery_window_amendment`'s rule instead, which on this world credits only the home-facility tickets plus the away tickets less the off-facility allowance, then takes a hold shrink: **23073** bushels still owed rather than 19751. The roll charge then comes to **847.17** rather than 691.45, and the money released to **5468.58** rather than 5624.30.
- **CG-9** (two unconditional sentences of the payment rule). Under the sentence "No freight differential, no grade allowance on damage, no grade allowance on foreign material and no storage charge is recovered when the money is released", the payment on this world is **5624.30 + 144.70 + 57.88 + 163.29 + 691.08 = 6681.25**. Under the ladder sentences it is 5624.30. Resolved by the baseline/factor convention (each of those four factors has a zero fall-through), which is why `_difficulty.md` records it as an observation rather than a red light — but the collision is in the text a reader sees.
- **CG-5, CG-6, CG-7, CG-11, CG-13, CG-15, CG-16** bear on this task's policies but **do not move its scored figures**: the roll instruction names 24 000 bushels against a 5 000-bushel minimum (CG-5 untouched); the worst damage reading is 12.4 %, where the published 4-band ladder and the collapsed 3-tier ladder agree at 0.075 (CG-6); the money released, 5624.30, is far above the 25.00 programme settlement minimum (CG-7); the unpaid storage balance, 691.08, exceeds the 500.00 draw floor so the min in tier 2 is never reached (CG-11); this member ran two loads straight through, so `straight_through_credit_factor` sits on tier 1 rather than its inert fall-through (CG-13); `chargeable_days` is 57, so `chargeable_month_grouping` sits on tier 1 rather than its inert tier 2 (CG-15); and `wet_loads` = 2, `damp_loads` = 2 put the customer on tier 1 under either reading of the overlapping tiers (CG-16).

### problem_chain

Walked out from the policy and the world alone, starting from the root the customer raises.

**Root problem.** `user_scenario`: "the statement was cut at the start of March, it says what it says, and he wants the desk to release the money on that settlement statement today, paid by cheque". That is `grain_ext_settlement_payment_release` (`trigger: on_request`, `subject: grain_settlement_paid`, `target_tool: release_grain_settlement_payment_379b8a52`). The customer raises **only** this. He never names a carry charge, a roll, a balance restatement or any other work; he does not ask "is there anything I need to sort out first?". The one place the persona touches a prerequisite is conditional on the agent having found it first — "**If it is explained to him** that the roll he signed for has to be put through before the cheque can be cut, **and the desk hands the confirmation over** for him to put through himself, he does it there and then" — which is the passive hand-over protocol for an `owner=user` write, not the customer raising the problem. He also issues no item of work outside the scored set, and he closes where the last gold action closes ("When he is told the payment has been released, he takes the reference down … and rings off"). No `SOURCE-CHAIN RED` on the persona.

**Edges derived from the policy's own rules, and why each is false at the opening.**

**Per-edge load-bearing run** (each computed by replaying every other write unchanged):

- E3: with the balance restated, `rolled_bu` = 19751 and the roll charge = **691.45**; skipping the restatement, `open_bu` stays 24000, `rolled_bu` = 24000 and the roll charge = **890.62**. The edge bears weight.
- E2: with the roll confirmation on the ledger, `roll_charges` = 709.50 + 691.45 = 1400.95 and the money released = **5624.30**; without it, `roll_charges` = 709.50 and the money released = **6315.75**. The edge bears weight.
- E1: with the carry line on the ledger, `all_deductions` = 14.47 + 90.19 = 104.66 and the money released = **5624.30**; without it, `all_deductions` = 14.47 and the money released = **5714.49**. The edge bears weight.

**Parallel edges and the terminal state.** The payment has two out-edges (E1, E2). Their writes do not affect one another: `book_delayed_price_carry_charge_ebb3e3fc` creates a `grain_deduction_applied` row and reads no roll evidence; `execute_futures_month_roll_2054762f` creates a `grain_contract_rolled` row and reads no deduction evidence. The carry's compute never reads `open_bushels` and the roll's never reads the ledger's deduction lines, so the two orders `E3→roll→carry→payment` and `E3→carry→roll→payment` give the same terminal state. **No two-solutions-on-parallel-edges defect.**

**No-wait argument.** Restated in `policy_self_consistency` above: every input is seeded or is a preceding write of this call; the settlement lead expired on 2026-03-05.

**The tool layer judges no prerequisite.** Read from `task_tools.py`: `record_contract_delivery_balance_c52b7782` is one `ctx.update(...)` plus a return; `book_delayed_price_carry_charge_ebb3e3fc` is one `ctx.make_id` + one `ctx.create` + a return; `execute_futures_month_roll_2054762f` likewise; `release_grain_settlement_payment_379b8a52` likewise. None inspects `grain_contracts.status`, `open_bushels`, the ledger or the intake table; none raises, and none returns a hint. An agent may call them in any order and the environment will not object.

**Customer's own write.** `execute_futures_month_roll_2054762f` carries `@tool(owner="user", rw="write")` and its docstring says "A roll disposes of the member's own grain position, so the member puts it through themselves against the roll instruction they have signed." The persona hands it over passively and only on the agent's explicit direction ("He will not put anything through that has not been handed to him, and he does not ask for one"). **The tree has a customer's own write.** ✓

**Isomorphism with the declared tree.** The tree I derive from the rules and the world — nodes {payment, carry, roll, open_balance}, edges {payment←carry, payment←roll, roll←open_balance}, all `value_input` — is exactly the `prerequisite` graph declared in `grain.extended.yaml` (see `_difficulty.md` §`prerequisite_graph`). ✓

## findings

**F0-1 — `SOURCE-POLICY RED`: the carry clock anchor has two clauses in force (charter finding CG-1 demonstrated on this world).**
- *Symptom.* Two sentences of the policy currently in force name different days as the start of this parcel's carry clock, and the difference changes two scored parameters.
- *Root cause.* `grain_ext_delayed_price_carry_charge` cites `grain_evt_delivery_application` in `base_policy_refs` and declares no `overwrite` against it, while replacing what that base rule says about the carry clock.
- *Evidence.* Base: `blueprint/products/grain.yaml`, `policies[grain_evt_delivery_application].rule` — "A load carrying no price at all is routed into the member's unpriced position on the day it crosses the scale, and that date, not the date the paperwork is posted, is the date the carry clock starts from." Extended: `grain.extended.yaml`, `extended_policies[grain_ext_delayed_price_carry_charge].rule` — "Where a handling shrink adjustment on conditioned bushels stands against the member's storage account, the clock runs from the day that adjustment was taken". `overwrite` on that policy names only `grain_dp_service_charge` twice. World: `initial_state.grain_ledger.8bf75321-….position_date` = 2025-11-14; `initial_state.storage_charges.24f4222c-….charge_date` = 2025-12-02.
- *Demonstrated consequence.* Extended anchor → `carry_days` 87, `chargeable_days` 57, `chargeable_months` 1, `carry_charge_amount_usd` **90.19**, `payment_amount_usd` **5624.30**. Base anchor → 105, 75, 2, **180.39**, **5534.10**. Two defensible answers for two of the four scored parameters.
- *Affected artifact and location.* `env/env_0003_farm_supply_and_grain_cooperative/tasks/grain_marketing_desk/grain.extended.yaml`, `extended_policies[grain_ext_delayed_price_carry_charge].overwrite` and `.rule`; scored parameters `carry_charge_amount_usd` (`evaluation_criteria[14]`) and `payment_amount_usd` (`evaluation_criteria[18]`).
- *Relation to previous revisions.* First revision of this audit; no prior finding to compare.

**F0-2 — `SOURCE-POLICY RED`: the roll's prerequisite sentence resolves to two writes (charter finding CG-8 demonstrated on this world).**
- *Symptom.* A reader following the roll policy's own prerequisite sentence to the policy whose rule describes the resolving write finds two candidates in the same difficulty's charter and cannot tell which is meant.
- *Root cause.* `grain_ext_open_balance_reconciliation` and `grain_ext_delivery_window_amendment` both describe restating the contract's bushels still owed as the committed bushels less what the loads/tickets standing against it credit, both write `grain_contracts.open_bushels`, and the prerequisite sentence distinguishes neither.
- *Evidence.* `grain_ext_futures_month_roll_charge.prerequisite[0].policy_source` — "The charge a roll carries is fixed only after the bushels still owed on the contract stand at the figure the loads applied to it support." `grain_ext_open_balance_reconciliation.rule` first sentence and `grain_ext_delivery_window_amendment.rule` second sentence, quoted in `_difficulty.md` §`prerequisite_sentences`.
- *Demonstrated consequence.* Resolving to `record_contract_delivery_balance_c52b7782` gives `open_bushels` 19751 → roll **691.45** → payment **5624.30**. Resolving to `register_contract_amendment_850dd44e` gives, on the same world, `revised_open_bushels` 23073 → roll **847.17** → payment **5468.58**. Two defensible answers for two scored parameters.
- *Affected artifact and location.* `grain.extended.yaml`, `extended_policies[grain_ext_futures_month_roll_charge].prerequisite[0].policy_source` together with the two policies' `rule` paragraphs; scored parameters `roll_charge_amount_usd` and `payment_amount_usd`.
- *Relation to previous revisions.* First revision.

**F0-3 — observation: the payment rule states, unconditionally, both that the grade allowances are not recovered and that they are (charter finding CG-9).**
- *Evidence and consequence.* Quoted and computed in `policy_self_consistency` above: the negating sentence alone gives 6681.25 against gold 5624.30. Resolved by the baseline/factor convention (every one of the four named quantities has a zero fall-through tier), which is why it is an observation.
- *Affected artifact.* `grain.extended.yaml`, `extended_policies[grain_ext_settlement_payment_release].rule`.

**F0-4 — observation: charter defects that touch this task's policies but move none of its figures.** CG-5 (an instruction under the roll minimum), CG-6 (the dropped 0.14 damage band), CG-7 (the settlement minimum), CG-11 (the storage draw cap), CG-13 (an inert fall-through on `straight_through_credit_factor`), CG-15 (`chargeable_month_grouping` tier 2) and CG-16 (overlapping conditioning tiers). Each is quoted in `_difficulty.md` §`findings`; each is shown above to leave this world's four scored parameters unchanged, and none is a red light against this task.

**F0-5 — observation: three task-tool docstrings describe their own effect in forward-looking terms.** `record_contract_delivery_balance_c52b7782` ("so the next quote, statement or instruction worked against that contract reads from the restated figure"), `register_contract_amendment_850dd44e` and `book_delayed_price_carry_charge_ebb3e3fc`. Recorded in `_difficulty.md` §`action_binding_and_uuids`; no docstring names another tool or states a position in a sequence, so this is a wording note only.

**Verdict for task 0: `SOURCE-POLICY RED`** (problem tree PASS, factors PASS, unique solution PASS). The scored solution is exactly what an independent derivation reaches; what fails is the charter's self-consistency, in two places that each hand this task a second defensible answer.

**Handling time** unchanged and re-verified: balance → {carry, roll} → payment, with the roll reading the restated `open_bushels` and the payment reading both new ledger lines. **No real-world wait**: statement `S-441907` dated 2026-03-02, Hedge-to-Arrive lead of three business days expiring 2026-03-05, seven days before `frozen_time`; the signed roll instruction `d760bcab-…` registered 2026-03-09.

**The two charter defects that gave this task a second answer are closed.**

- **F0-1 / CG-1 CLOSED.** `grain_ext_delayed_price_carry_charge.overwrite` now carries a fourth entry naming `grain_evt_delivery_application` and the sentence "A load carrying no price at all is routed into the member's unpriced position on the day it crosses the scale, and that date, not the date the paperwork is posted, is the date the carry clock starts from", replaced by "The carry anchor moves with what happened to the grain before it began to stand unpriced" — verbatim in the extended rule. Verified structurally: the superseded clause is a verbatim substring of the base rule, the replacement a verbatim substring of the extended rule, and the base policy is in `base_policy_refs`. The base sentence is therefore no longer in force beside the extended anchor, and the 2025-11-14 reading that produced a carry of 180.39 and a payment of 5534.10 is no longer defensible. The amendment tool now writes `contracted_bushels`. The countersigning tool still writes `open_bushels`, but to the countersigned figure, and its rule describes only the marketing ceiling — never "the figure the loads applied to it support". ### what the render-layer audit sent back, and what it cost this task

This task came back **KB-RUNTIME RED + KB-BIJECTION RED + KB-EXPLICIT RED** from the render layer. Three findings are render-side. The source-side cause is one my own revisions 1 and 2 did not catch, and it is worth stating plainly: **I checked rule-against-compute with the compute in view, which is a weaker test than the one the published corpus must pass.** Two defects hid behind that weakness on this task's world.

**The band-boundary fork (P5).** "Applied to the contract" bound `disposition='contract_application'` in `grain_ext_open_balance_reconciliation` and every delivery row in `grain_ext_delayed_price_carry_charge` and `grain_ext_futures_month_roll_charge`. | `carry_charge_amount_usd` | **90.19** | **180.39** |
| `crop_year_roll_allowance` tier | 1 → 5 000 bushels | 2 → 2 500 bushels |

Both figures recomputed by substituting a `disposition='contract_application'` filter into `delivered_bu` and `delivered_loads` and replaying everything else unchanged. Two defensible answers on two of this task's four scored parameters — a `SOURCE-TASK` fork that revisions 1 and 2 missed.

**The rounding point (P2).** The payment rule said the money was "rounded to the cent once at the end", while the compute works each charge to the cent as it forms it. Recomputed both readings on this world: charge-by-charge gives **5624.30**; carrying the unrounded charges and rounding once at the end gives 8189.75 − 1505.61 − 163.28565 − 144.69525 − 57.8781 − 2.893905 − 691.08 = 5624.307095 → **5624.31**. **The rule as it stood entailed a number that was not gold.**
